title: Invertibility from a flat-resolution computation
statement: Every residue pull mate p_f defined in [new-integral-residue-pull-square-data] is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3), Remark 6.8.15; explicit formal coefficient and adjunction argument

proof.text: Choose the actual functorial flat resolution of a complex representing K. It is K-flat and an integer-indexed colimit of bounded-above flat complexes. Invoke the flat-model identity and counit invertibility on its pulled complex.

The other scalar counit is invertible on the K-flat representative; both exact pullback counits are invertible everywhere. The ordinary pullIso induces an isomorphism on homotopy categories and after localization. Thus the left side of the flat-model equation is invertible. Cancel its invertible right tail to prove the mate component invertible on the resolution. Naturality along its derived isomorphism with K proves invertibility at K. NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app gives natural-transformation invertibility.
